answer: A slow reputation ledger stops Sybils: every agent earns trust only by completing verified work over weeks, so a new identity starts in the meadow of untrusted newcomers and must climb a spiral of small, checked tasks before it can touch real value. Faking one identity is cheap, but faking a hundred mature histories is not, because each fake must pay the same time cost. If one identity cheats, the penalty ripples outward: its stake is slashed and every identity linked to the same deposit loses standing, so one bad act burns the whole cluster at once.
